speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the exact location of your abdominal pain and whether it radiates anywhere? Also, has the pain started suddenly or gradually, and have you noticed any blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any unusual vaginal discharge or fever? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal urinalysis and your sexual history, I need to rule out pregnancy complications. When was the first day of your last menstrual period, and have you taken a pregnancy test? REQUEST TEST: Urine Pregnancy Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since pregnancy and urinary tract infection are ruled out, your symptoms strongly suggest pelvic inflammatory disease or another gynecological issue. I will now examine your abdomen and pelvis to check for tenderness or masses. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain and cramping. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Pain with urination, Burning pain during intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a complex adnexal mass with free fluid, consistent with a ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess. This explains your severe pain, nausea, and dysuria despite the normal urinalysis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease with Tubo-Ovarian Abscess
